full_judgment:
The writ-petitioners are law abiding citizens and come from respectable Muslim families. One Mr Ahsan Habib applied to the Government for allotment of Khas land within Cox's Bazar's Hotel/Motel Zone for construction of a hotel. The Government allotted 1.00 acre of land initially but the land was submerged in water. Subsequently, the Government allotted Plot No. 13 (Kolatoli Road) on 26-1-2003 by a lease deed for a period of 99 years. Thereafter, the lessee Mr Habib filed an application before the Deputy Commissioner of Cox's Bazar seeking permission to transfer the allotted land in favour of the writ-petitioners. The application was allowed and the writ-petitioners deposited transfer fees on 13-7-2006. Thereafter, on 27-6-2006 transfer deed had been executed and registered. The writ-petitioners thereafter mutated the land in their names. After that, the writ-petitioners obtained possession of the land and constructed boundary walls and proceeded with the construction work. The writ-petitioners, in one part of the land constructed a Motel which was rented out to the tourists. Soon thereafter, the Care-taker Government took over charge. As a result, due to unavoidable circumstances, the construction work had to be suspended temporarily. 

 12. One Mohammad Ahsan Habib applied to the Government for allotment of khas land within Cox's Bazar Hotel/Motel Zone for construction of a Hotel. The Government allotted 1 (one) acre of land initially but the land was submerged in water. Later the Government allotted plot No.13 (Kolatoli Road) on 26-1-2003. The lessee filed an application before the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar, seeking permission to transfer the allotted land in favour of the writ-petitioners. The application was allowed and the writ-petitioners deposited transfer fees on 13-7-2006. After that, the transfer deed was executed and registered on 27-6-2006. In 2009, the writ petitioners obtained No objection Certificate from Civil Aviation Authority for construction of the hotel. The writ-petitioners also prepared plan and submitted the same with the Paurashova which approved it on 19-6-2006. They filed applications to the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and the Ministry of Land seeking 3 years extension for completion of the project. But no decision on those applications had been communicated to the petitioners. After that, writ-respondent No. 2 abruptly issued the order dated 12-1-2010 (impugned before the High Court Division) informing the writ-petitioners that the lease agreement has been cancelled and directed the writ-petitioners to hand over the land to the Government.
